title: Meet the Melon Heads: West Michigan's Creepiest Cryptid
excerpt: Tiny creatures with giant heads supposedly roam the woods near Holland and Saugatuck. Here’s the legend behind them.
content:
People who know me know I appreciate folklore and cryptids. I have a Bigfoot statue next to my computer; Nessie from Loch Ness will forever have a special spot in my heart thanks to a Scooby-Doo special I watched as a kid, and don't even get me started on the Dogman song: banger.

Get our free mobile app

But what if I told you there was a cryptid said to be here in West Michigan?  Small creatures with abnormally large, bulbous heads said to prowl the woods around Holland and Saugatuck, spawning years of stories, personal accounts, and even movies about the creatures known as the Melon Heads. 

The Melon Heads of West Michigan

The Melon Heads story centers on the Felt Mansion in Holland. It's rumored a nearby asylum once housed children with hydrocephalus; whether they escaped or were abandoned, the children with abnormally large heads found their way into the surrounding woods.

READ MORE: 11 Bigfoot Sightings Reported in West Michigan

Some versions say they were just children; others say they were feral creatures with fangs and claws. Either way, roaming the woods at night was not recommended. Legends of the Melon Heads have spread to other states, including Ohio and Connecticut, and have spurred both a 2011 and 2024 film. But do these tales have any merit?

The Melon Heads - Real or Fiction?

Really, the only constants in the story are the head size and the Felt Mansion, and according to WMUK, it's nothing but a story. The biggest red flag in these tales, as pointed out by both Jim Hayden, the public information officer for Laketown Township, and the Allegan County Historical Society, is that no record exists of an asylum ever operating in the region, let alone at the Felt Mansion. Felt Mansion has been many things over time, but never an asylum.

That hasn't stopped the mansion from leaning into the spookiness surrounding it. Each year, the Felt Mansion hosts haunted tours around Halloween.

The east side of the state has a similar cryptid of its own, known as the Nain Rouge, aka the Devil of Detroit, said to be a small red demon seen before tragic events.

According to the book "The United States Cryptids: A Tour of American Myths and Monsters" by J.W. Ocker, locals attempted to appease the Nain Rouge in 2010 by hosting the "Marche Du Nain Rouge", a parade in the devil's honor as an attempt to end Detroit's economic struggles.
